DEFINITIONS & POSSIBLE CASE
INDEPENDENT CLAUSE
DEPENDENT CLAUSE
1
They can exist alone.
I would pay a ´private college...
IF I had the money.
2
They need another clause to exist.
She could call Mark...
IF she wanted to.
3
Switching Clauses
If they flunked the test ,
Their parents would ground them for life.
To Consider

The use of would / could is commonly seen here to express the possibility about something.
The dependent clauses are used in simple past tense.
When the IF clause is the first one, it needs to be separated by a comma (,) from the other clause.
The correct form to use is: If I were...
Conditionals link two different clauses as we learned in the last unit. Second conditional links a possibility with a situation unlikely to happen.

slideDifferences.nativeText:
We can use the first conditional aiming the following functions or aspects
To consider 
Second Conditional can also be used to give advice to people. E.G:
If I were you, I would not do that.
Functions
Examples
1
Considering life decisions
If I were a doctor, I would be a plastic surgeon.
She would definitely choose Mike if she ever got married.
2
Being in someone else’s shoes.
I would say yes if I were her.
If he were a professional, they would probably hire him.

slideDifferences.nativeText:
What if...

Have you ever wondered what you would do if you were rich? I have. If I were rich, I would be using my money to start helping people and not by giving them money per se but giving the opportunities to study or prepare themselves. I would also open a foundation to help people develop their skills if they were willing to perfect and offer what they do. For sure, I would not use it just for that, but If I had enough money, I would definitely travel to meet new places and people. Haven’t you given a thought? If I were you, I would start considering it just in case.

texts: Have you ever wondered what you would do if you were rich? I have. If I were rich, I would be using my money to start helping people and not by giving them money per se but giving the opportunities to study or prepare themselves. I would also open a foundation to help people develop their skills if they were willing to perfect and offer what they do. For sure, I would not use it just for that, but If I had enough money, I would definitely travel to meet new places and people. Haven’t you given a thought? If I were you, I would start considering it just in case.
